title: Direct-cessation weaning of high-flow nasal cannula for infants with bronchiolitis: a ward quality improvement project
abstract: Problem: infants with bronchiolitis spent a median of 52 hours on high flow on a general pediatric ward, with weaning varying by attending. Intervention: a direct-cessation protocol for infants aged 8 weeks or older, tested in three PDSA cycles. Measures: weekly median time on high flow, with re-escalation, PICU transfer and 7-day readmission as balancing measures. Results will be reported after the season.
introduction: Direct cessation shortened time on high flow in a trial and a ward report, but the evidence for infants younger than 8 weeks conflicts, and night delivery of weaning checks is unreliable.
methods: Model for Improvement with the previous season as baseline and three cycles from November 2026 to March 2027. Run chart rules and a safety stopping rule were fixed in advance; infants under 8 weeks continued stepwise weaning and were followed descriptively. The project was screened as quality improvement.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the run chart, the balancing measures, night adherence and the descriptive results for infants under 8 weeks.
discussion: The discussion will weigh any shift in time on high flow against the safety measures and state what the ward keeps; it will not claim safety for infants under 8 weeks.
limitations: Single ward, one season, historical baseline, and small numbers for safety outcomes.
conclusion: To be written after the season; limited to infants aged 8 weeks or older on this ward.
summary: SQUIRE-structured draft with results left empty until the season ends.
